claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has a uniform, fine lamellar structure.
A crack-free Y- and Hf-co-doped AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA coating can be prepared by laser cladding.
The cited laser-cladding process can deposit the YHf-EHEA layer specifically onto a bulk AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA substrate.
Y and Hf co-doping improves the thermal stability of laser-cladded AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA at 900 °C.
Y and Hf co-doping reduces grain growth during a 900 °C, 10-hour heat treatment relative to an undoped EHEA coating.
Y and Hf co-doping promotes formation of a thermally stable, adherent oxide scale.
The protective scale contains Y-rich and Hf-rich oxides.
The oxide scale acts as a barrier to corrosive species.
Formation of the oxide scale is the mechanism that suppresses grain coarsening.
Y and Hf co-doping improves resistance to hot-corrosion oxide-scale spallation.
The YHf-doped coating will have a lower oxide-scale spallation area than the undoped coating.
The YHf-doped coating will retain strength and ductility better during long-term loading.
The coating will improve performance under extreme or cyclic temperature fluctuations.
The improvement in thermal stability and corrosion resistance will be statistically significant.
Undoped laser-cladded AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA undergoes grain coarsening at 900 °C.
Undoped AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA has limited hot-corrosion resistance under the stated molten-salt conditions.
The relevant hot-corrosion environment is approximately 900 °C with 75% Na2SO4 and 25% NaCl molten salts.
Room-temperature cyclic mechanical loading adequately simulates creep and cyclic thermal fluctuations.
Laser cladding can reliably produce a uniform YHf-doped coating on the EHEA substrate.

contradictions.description: The predicted lower spallation area agrees with the evidence record's verbal conclusion, but the record's reported values are 14.98% for YHf-EHEA and 5.67% for EHEA, numerically indicating greater rather than lower spallation for the doped coating.

The stated target includes cyclic thermal fluctuations and creep, but the experiment substitutes parallel room-temperature cyclic mechanical loading without thermal cycling or a defined sustained-load creep test.

The baseline is described as unmodified bulk EHEA and the prediction permits comparison with either an uncoated or standard coated surface, whereas the experiment includes only a standard laser-cladded EHEA coating as the control.
